description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/chat.rs:523
Issue: The list of server-set Chat fields that cannot be patched is defined as a hardcoded const &[&str] slice: CHAT_READONLY = ["id", "createdAt", "unreadCount", "pinnedMessageIds"]. The same fields are defined structurally on the Chat type in jmap-chat-types. When a new server-set field is added to Chat, a developer must also add it to CHAT_READONLY. There is no compiler signal if they forget. A similar pattern exists in crate-jmap-mail-server/src/helpers.rs (IMMUTABLE_EMAIL_FIELDS).
Risk: Adding a server-set field to Chat and forgetting CHAT_READONLY means clients can write to it. This is a security and data-integrity issue, not just an ergonomics issue. The pattern will be replicated in every new object type's set handler.
Fix: Document the invariant that CHAT_READONLY must stay in sync with server-set fields in the Chat struct, with a reference to the struct definition. Ideally, expose a method on the Chat type (or a trait) that returns the set of server-set field names, so there is a single source of truth. A compile-time test that constructs a full Chat and verifies every server-set field key appears in the list would also catch drift.
title: CHAT_READONLY list for update validation is not compiler-enforced
